boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Whitestone Hill record (September 3-5, 1863) in Operations Against the Sioux in North Dakota [July 1863]. Sully's march from the Little Cheyenne from August 21 and his return to Fort Pierre are context; the frozen campaign label reads July 1863 although the record is dated September. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives the Northwestern Expedition as 600-700 and the Santee, Yankton, Cut-heads, Hunkpapa, Teton and Blackfeet as 1,200-1,500; the stored bounds are 600 and 600 and 1,200 and 1,200, not the text's ranges. The live field reads 0. Sully says 600 to 700 of his men were actually engaged and gives House's battalion 300; the camp mustered at least 1,200 warriors by the Indians' account and over 1,500 by his command's. House reports 400 lodges and Sully over 400 (some say 600, read '000').
claims.rationale: Engaged and estimated figures, all for September 3: 600 to 700 of Sully's men engaged (his postscript), House's 300 on the approach, and the camp's 1,200 (prisoners' statement) or 1,500 (his command's estimate). No account by the Dakota bands was inspected; their numbers, aims and losses come from their opponents' estimates, prisoners' or scouts' statements relayed by them, or the NPS summary. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Sully sent House's battalion ahead to find the Indians and report a large camp; the guide bore off to the left and came on the camp, whose people, prisoners said, believed Sully was still going up the Missouri. House's guide reported the camp 3 miles off about 3 p.m.; the guide La Framboise rode more than 10 miles back to Sully, reaching him a little after 4.
claims.rationale: Knowledge attributed in interested reports and relayed prisoners' statements; no message log inspected.

claims.value: The frozen US commander is Brigadier General Alfred Sully. The frozen and live Native American commander is Inkpaduta (no rank; the live page tags him [CS], not adopted); none of the inspected reports names him, so his role is not established here. Sully ordered Furnas's Second Nebraska to the right and Wilson's Sixth Iowa to the left and charged the center himself; House's battalion first found and tried to hold the camp. Hall commanded the September 5 scouting party.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sully says the Indians resisted desperately, then broke and fled, and that he gave them one of the most severe punishments they had received; he took 156 prisoners, 32 men and 124 women and children. On September 5 about 300 Indians attacked Hall's party of 27, which retreated to camp faster than ordered.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The September 5 skirmish is within the frozen interval and is kept separate from the September 3 action.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 822 (US 72; I 750); the live field reads 620 (US 70; CS 550). Sully reports his killed as 20 and wounded 38 as far as ascertained; he puts the Indian dead left on the field or found by scouts at 100, his officers and guides at not less than 150, and Indian reports at over 200. House says about 100 were killed. Hall lost 6 men killed on September 5 and says 6 Indians were killed. The compiled return's table is not present in the OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen 750 is not traced; prisoners are not casualties of the kind counted in the frozen table unless it says so.

open_questions: Wilson's and Furnas's reports (read in part), the compiled return's table, the Dakota bands' account, the question whether later writers characterize the action differently (no inspected source here does), and maps remain deferred. Hall's report is the targeted follow-up for the September 5 skirmish.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Sully's September 11, 1863 report and House's undated September report (Sixth Iowa) are interested accounts; Hall's report on September 5 is a separate family used as the follow-up. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
